title: Stats: India's highest away total comes with a historic Test first
excerpt: For the first time in the history of Test cricket, a team had 50-plus stands for each of the first seven wickets in an innings
author: Roshan Gede
body: All the stats highlights from Day 4 of the ongoing first Test between New Zealand and India in Wellington.
India breach 700 for the fifth time

720/9d recorded by India is now their third-highest total in Test cricket, and their highest in an away Test. It is also the highest innings total against New Zealand in Tests, bettering 660/5d by the West Indies at the same venue in 1995.
Furthermore, it’s the highest team total in New Zealand, surpassing 715/6d by the hosts against Bangladesh in Hamilton in 2019.

5 - This was India’s 5th 700-plus total in Tests, a number exceeded only by Sri Lanka (7). England, Australia and the West Indies have got four each, while Pakistan and New Zealand have got two and one respectively.
India’s previous highest Test score against the Blackcaps was 583/7d in Ahmedabad in 1999. It was their second 500-plus total in New Zealand after 520 all-out at Hamilton in 2009.

Interestingly, India had totalled 722 in four innings combined on their last Test tour of New Zealand in 2020: 165 and 191 in the first Test in Wellington, followed by 242 and 124 in Christchurch. They almost bettered that in a single innings this time around.
1 - For the first time in the history of Test cricket, a team had 50-plus stands for each of the first seven wickets in an innings.

Overall, India’s seven 50-plus stands is the joint second-most in a Test innings, alongside as many for Australia in Sydney during the Ashes 2025/26. India hold the overall record with eight against England at The Oval in 2007.
It was also just the second instance of each of a team’s top five scoring 80 or more in a Test innings. The previous too, had come against New Zealand - by Pakistan (566/3d) at Abu Dhabi in 2014.
Pant's six-hitting surge and a perfect SENA tons set
108 sixes for Rishabh Pant in Tests now puts him second only to Ben Stokes (138) in the format. He surpassed Brendon McCullum’s 107 during his stroke-filled 128.

14 sixes by India is their joint third-most in a Test innings alongside as many against South Africa in Visakhapatnam in 2019. They had hit 18 against England in Rajkot in 2024, and 15 against Sri Lanka in Brabourne in 2009.
9 - This was Pant’s ninth Test ton, taking him past England’s Les Ames for the third-most tons as a designated wicketkeeper in Tests; only Adam Gilchrist (17) and Andy Flower (12) have more.

6 - The left-hander also became the sixth Indian with a Test hundred in each of the four SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia). Mohammad Azharuddin, Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid and Virat Kohli were the first four, before KL Rahul joined this select list on Saturday. Saeed Anwar, Younis Khan and Kumar Sangakkara are the other sub-continent batters in this club. Pant is the only batter in this list to have scored all those hundreds as a designated wicketkeeper.
A day to forget for Duffy and Latham
1/201 - Jacob Duffy's 1/201 is the second-most runs conceded by a New Zealand bowler in a Test innings, only behind 1/229 by Stephen Boock against Pakistan in Auckland in 1989.

He is the second bowler to concede 200-plus in an innings at more than run-a-ball in Test cricket history (1/201 in 33 overs at an ER of 6.09), after Zahid Mahmood (PAK), who returned 4/235 in 33 overs against England at Rawalpindi in 2022.
Most runs conceded by a New Zealand bowler in a Test innings

3 - Tom Latham became the third New Zealand captain to bag a pair in a Test match, falling to Jasprit Bumrah in the opening over in both innings. The previous two were Harry Cave (against West Indies, Dunedin, 1956) and Stephen Fleming (against Australia, Hobart, 1997).
This was the eighth instance of a New Zealand opener bagging a pair in a Test, and the second against India after Tim McIntosh in Ahmedabad in 2010.

16 - Latham now has 17 ducks in Tests, 16 as an opener. The latter is the joint third-most among openers in the format, alongside as many for Marvan Atapattu, and only behind 19 for Kraigg Brathwaite and 17 for Mike Atherton.

3 - Bumrah became the third Indian bowler to bag a wicket in the first over in both innings of a Test match, after S Sreesanth and Zaheer Khan. Sreesanth had dismissed Chris Gayle twice at Kingston in 2006, while Zaheer got the better of Javed Omar on the very first ball in both innings at Mirpur in 2007.
